prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a parking lot collision in Pasadena, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1286; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to the accident, if that's alright.
Q: That's fine, we'll keep identifying details to a minimum. Can you describe where the collision happened?
A: It was in a parking lot at a shopping center in Pasadena, Texas. I was pulling out of a space near the front entrance.
Q: What were you doing right before the impact?
A: I had checked my mirror, saw nothing coming, and started backing out slowly. I was maybe going five miles an hour.
Q: What happened next?
A: A vehicle came down the lane between the rows and hit the rear passenger side of my car. I didn't see it coming because a delivery van was parked on that side and blocked the view.
Q: Did you have any contact with the other driver before or after the collision?
A: Just a brief exchange. They said they were in a hurry and didn't see me. We exchanged insurance information and that was it.
Q: Did you feel any injury at the time?
A: My right wrist hurt right away, but I thought it was just a jolt. I hit the steering wheel and then the door frame. By the evening it was swollen and I could barely grip anything.
Q: Have you been seen by a doctor?
A: Yes, I went to urgent care the next day and they took X-rays. The doctor told me the wrist was fractured and I'd need a splint and a follow-up with a specialist.
Q: Were you able to drive your vehicle afterward?
A: It was driveable, but the back panel was crushed and the rear tire was rubbing. I had it towed to a repair shop.
Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about the accident?
A: Only that I've never had an accident like this before, and I'm worried about how long my recovery will take and whether I'll lose work time.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
A: Okay, thanks.
